title: Fire station bills tied to Methodist church rezoning
summary: A committee voted nine to zero to recommend Bill 94-2026 as amended, which would rezone Lahaina United Methodist Church land from residential to public/quasi-public use. A land use zoning map and a committee report are still needed before first reading. The church burned down in August 2023 and wants to rebuild.

boards.name: Disaster Recovery, International Affairs, and Planning Committee

timeline.text: A land use zoning map and a committee report are needed before the bill moves to first reading.

timeline.text: The pastor said the church would likely be interested in combining the lots, pending its church council's approval.

timeline.text: The public works director said combining the two lots could cost about $5,000 to $10,000.

timeline.text: The planning department supports the rezoning because it matches past uses and the community plan.

timeline.text: No one signed up for public testimony.

timeline.text: The Office of Recovery said required improvements can be handled at the building permit stage.

timeline.text: The church's deed shows the land is about 3.26 acres, so the bill needed an amendment.

timeline.text: Lahaina United Methodist Church, which burned down in August 2023, is seeking a rezoning so it can rebuild.
